text:
infra-bot: ALERT: Serving runtime pool gpu-pool-7 exhibiting repeated container crashes (OOM + device address validation failures). 15% of requests failing with 502 over last 3m. Auto-eviction triggered. (alert_id=INC-3250009999)

marta (oncall): grabbing this. seeing lots of container restarts on gpu-node-19. pods in CrashLoopBackOff. any queued deploys? @deploy-bot

deploy-bot: No active deploys in last 10m. Last deploy: model-reload v2.4 at 3250007000 (success). Canary traffic on node-19.

leo (infra): I'm seeing repeated kernel logs referencing a pointer validation failure in device-mm path on node-19. Not exactly the usual OOM pattern. Pasting dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1423.112345] deviceaddr_check: parity fail at 0x7f3a2c1b0000
[ 1423.112347] gpu-chan 4: ptr slip detected, mm pagewalk invalid
[ 1423.112349] BUG: bad pointer in device address translation
[ 1423.112350] task: serving-runtime pid: 52114 name: runtime-service
```

raj (sre): "ptr slip"? that's a new phrasing, maybe kernel reported different symbol across distros. How many nodes affected?

leo (infra): so far only gpu-node-19 and gpu-node-20 (same hostclass, same kernel 5.15.88-custom). Other pools on different kernels OK.

marta (oncall): customers impacted? CS, can you surface any customer errors/EScalations? @customer-success

customer-success: We're getting elevated 502s for a few mid-market customers in eu-west-1. No P1 tickets yet but one customer reported latency spikes and reconnects. We'll open incident customer notes after triage.

dana (eng-runtime): on it. logs from runtime show repeated CUDA driver errors before the crash:
```
E CudaDriver: cuLaunchKernel: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x00007f3a2c1b
E Runtime: failed to pin buffer: devaddr validation failed
```

marta (oncall): immediate mitigations: cordon gpu-node-19 and gpu-node-20 to stop new pods, scale down pool to healthy nodes, enable degrade-route to fallback CPU-pool for critical routes. Can someone run the cordon now? @leo

leo (infra): cordoning nodes now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-19,gpu-node-20` -> done. Evicting non-critical pods. Scaling serving runtime pool to remove those nodes from rotation.

marta (oncall): good. dana, can you add an automatic fallback (model variant with CPU runtime) for customer-critical routes? Use canary revert policy.

dana (eng-runtime): pushing fallback rule: route-based fallback for /generate -> cpu-quantized-variant. Patching routing config. Watch for regression in quality.

raj (sre): while we reduce blast radius, let's collect full artifacts for root cause. Actions:
- collect dmesg, `journalctl -u runtime`, `kubectl describe pod` for crashed pods
- `nvidia-smi -q` and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` output
- container core dumps (if any) and driver logs

marta (oncall): I'll take core dumps and system journal. @dana please collect runtime traces and ray KV cache state.

infra-bot: NOTE: automatic node eviction occurred due to repeated process crashes. Rolling-pool fallback activated for 8 pods.

leo (infra): attaching quick checks: `uname -a` -> linux node-19 5.15.88-custom #42; seccomp profile default. SMMU enabled in kernel boot args. GPU driver nvidia 525.60.11.

dana (eng-runtime): I see repeated failures when model sequence length > 1024 (longer contexts). The runtime tries to pin larger buffers; kernel complains during the device translation. Could be a pagewalk race under high KV cache pressure.

raj (sre): interesting. any recent kernel upgrades or configuration drift on that hostclass? @leo

leo (infra): last kernel upgrade was 5.15.88-custom deployed 2 weeks ago to that hostclass. We did not roll it to other hostclasses. Rolling back kernel is invasive; prefer to hotpatch if possible.

marta (oncall): can we reduce memory pressure on GPU by lowering batch sizes on affected nodes and lowering prefetch cache? Dana, can runtime throttle batching/prefetch per-node?

dana (eng-runtime): yes. Pushing runtime config overrides to affected node labels: `batch_size: 1`, `kv_prefetch: false`, `max_seq: 1024`. Applying now.

marta (oncall): monitor error rate.

(4m later)

dana (eng-runtime): after throttle: crash frequency dropped from once/min -> once/30m. Error type still device addr validation but less frequent. Looks correlated to batch/prefetch.

raj (sre): good. that's a strong signal this is a workload-induced race. Still need kernel-side fix.

leo (infra): I'm going to prepare a node-level mitigations playbook: 1) disable SMMU, 2) apply kernel patch if available, 3) rollback kernel to 5.15.76 for that hostclass. Trying 1) first: toggling kernel boot arg to disable smmu is disruptive — will require reboot.

marta (oncall): we should only reboot if we have capacity. For now keep cordon and throttles; inform customers of mitigations.

customer-success: Drafting message: "We've observed intermittent backend errors caused by a low-level device translation issue on a small subset of GPU nodes. We've cordoned affected hosts and routed traffic to healthy capacity. We're monitoring and will follow up with technical details." Will send to impacted customers in 30 min.

dana (eng-runtime): also we can push a runtime-level safety: when device addr validation fails, fallback to a safe memcpy path that avoids pinned devmem (slower but prevents crash). I can roll a hotfix to canary.

marta (oncall): please do that. prioritize safety over perf. @dana

dana (eng-runtime): hotfix pushed to canary (runtime-safety-fallback). Rolling to 5% of traffic on unaffected nodes first.

deploy-bot: rollout started: runtime-safety-fallback -> canary (5% traffic) at 3250011000.

(10m)

dana (eng-runtime): canary looks stable, no regression on unrelated paths. I'll expand to 25% and target affected pool if safe.

raj (sre): once safety-fallback is at scale, we can consider evacuating and rebooting nodes to disable SMMU if needed.

leo (infra): I've queued a kernel rollback to 5.15.76 for a single canary node in the hostclass (gpu-node-21) to validate rollback impact. Scheduling maintenance window for rolling reboots if it passes.

marta (oncall): handoff: I'm going to sleep-mode in 45m. Next oncall please pick up at 3250014800. @raj you'll be primary follow-up, @leo will drive infra changes, @dana runtime. I'll send handoff note including customer list.

raj (sre): ack. I'll be standing by. Will collect RCA artifacts and attach to ticket INC-3250009999.

marta (oncall): posting interim incident summary to #incidents-summary and pinging customer-success for update.

customer-success: Message queued and will be sent after review. No escalations yet.

infra-bot: ACTION: create bug ticket in infra-kernel for "device address translation race leading to pointer validation failures under heavy KV prefetch". Ticket INFRA-8472 created.

dana (eng-runtime): note for follow-up: add telemetry to capture buffer sizes + sequence length at time of device validation error for better repro.

marta (oncall): incident status -> mitigated (reduced error rate, fallbacks applied). Next steps: kernel rollback/patch, runtime hotfix expansion, customer followups, RCA. Handoff to @raj at 3250014800.

raj (sre): taking over at 3250014800. Packing artifacts, will coordinate kernel rollback if we get clean canary results. Keep the channel open for further updates.

(End of thread)
